gap: No result ChatGPT got puts today's maker-store prices next to measured energy for the 1.5V Li-ion AA field. The XTAR CLR 4300 tested highest in Charge-Test's lab at 3,703 mWh and lists at $25.99 on xtardirect.com, $1 more than the XTAR 4150 (3,420 mWh, $24.99). The CLR 4300 also needs a compatible XTAR charger, which the cards don't price: the L4 Pro is $15.90.
standout_why: Charge-Test (cited) has the measured-energy ranking but no prices. xtar.cc gives third-party measurements but no prices. Light and Matter (cited) prices only EBL ($24.99 for 8 cells with a charger, $29.49 without). RedRecs lists Amazon prices without pack sizes and doesn't say which picks are lithium. None of them prices the charger the CLR 4300 needs or shows that EBL's own store sells 8 cells plus a charger ($29.99) for less than its 4-pack ($31.48). The pairing is new but only partly so. I couldn't confirm the pack counts behind the store prices, so I can't give a solid cost per Wh.
decides: It supports ChatGPT's capacity pick, the XTAR CLR 4300: it measured 8% more energy than the XTAR 4150 (3,703 vs 3,420 mWh, Charge-Test) for $1 more on the maker's store. A shopper without an XTAR charger should budget for the $15.90 L4 Pro. That brings the CLR 4300 to $41.89, the same range as the Pale Blue 8-pack ChatGPT showed at $41.99. EBL stays the budget option only if bought as the 8-cell-plus-charger bundle ($29.99), not the $31.48 4-pack. EBL loses for flash and other high-drain use: Light and Matter measured 10.72 s and 17.55 s full-power recycle times, against 2.23–2.77 s for NiMH and alkaline. Our only listed lithium AA is the XTAR 4150 8-pack on Amazon; the eneloop and Tenergy cells we list are NiMH and don't answer a lithium question.
